page.claims_line: The paper's main claim holds on the simulated data: the OR gate wins for the feed-forward loop and AND(gA+, gD-) wins for gC. Its error figures and its haematopoietic network do not come back; the causes are the unstated informative prior, pseudo time scale and noise settings, and the unstated choice of cells and orderings on the GMP and CLP pathways.
came_back: Moignard's quality control on their Supplementary Table 3 leaves exactly the paper's 597 cells and its five per-type counts.
Supplementary Table 10 prints 100.9 for the qPCR data. Its Figure 32A puts the best width at 10 to the power 0.9, and so does our curve. 100.9 flattens the map.
GENIE3 with extra-trees gives 29 edges above 0.08, and 28 of them are the 30 of Fig. 7C.
The supplement's own traces give the system noise: 2 for the feed-forward loop and about 6 for the toggle switch.
AIC and thermodynamic integration pick the OR gate with gX activating and gY repressing, by Bayes factors far above 100.
Our MAP estimates put alpha near 64 and lambda near 0.16, as Fig. 3 does, with their ratio near 400.
Four eigenvalues stand out and the cells form an X with four branches, as in supp. Fig. 6 and Fig. 1B.

page.matched_intro: The paper's figures are vector drawings. We read each panel's axes from its tick labels in the PDF and draw our curves on the same pixel grid at 600 dpi, in the published colours. A score is the share of the published line within 2 px of ours, and of ours within 2 px of the published line; the smaller counts.
matched: The two simulated systems, rerun from their equations with noise read from the supplement's traces, and the Moignard 2013 qPCR data. Diffusion maps, Wanderlust, GENIE3, the ODE models, MCMC and thermodynamic integration rebuilt in Python.
One linear map per axis from the tick labels of the vector figure; the plotted curves and points read out of the same PDF give the paper's numbers where it prints none.
The view of Fig. 7B (a linear projection of our three components that sends each cell type's centre to the published one) and GENIE3's tree method (from a grid of four).
Each panel is also scored with a wrong input (another panel's curve) and near misses (a 1% shift, amplitude x 1.05). A panel agrees only when ours beats them and passes 90%.
Overlay: ink is the paper only, light green is ours only, dark green is both. Difference: darker means a larger grey-level difference.
page.closing: The framework comes back from the paper alone. Its logic calls on the simulated data come back; its numbers and the haematopoietic network do not, because the settings behind them were never written down.
